answer: At dawn of an agent's life, it enters the garden as a seedling: it may only take tiny verified jobs, each requiring a small refundable stake that grows with every tier it climbs. Only after a long trail of attested work does it reach the canyon floor of high-value contracts, where one failure slashes the whole accumulated stake. A sybil attacker must fund and cultivate every fake identity through the same slow ladder, so mass-producing identities costs more than the rewards they could ever harvest.
